advisor.standby.recovery_conflicts.title: Standby queries on {database} are cancelled by WAL replay
advisor.standby.recovery_conflicts.detai: Since the previous scrape, replay on this standby cancelled queries of database {database} that conflicted with the changes it applied ({counted}). Each one fails with "canceling statement due to conflict with recovery".{adv_active_logicalslot, select, true { active_logicalslot: a logical slot on the standby was invalidated because the primary removed rows its decoding needs; hot_standby_feedback = on with a physical slot between primary and standby prevents it.} other {}}{adv_bufferpin, select, true { bufferpin: replay waited for a page a standby query kept pinned.} other {}}{adv_deadlock, select, true { deadlock: a standby query and replay waited for each other on a buffer pin.} other {}}{adv_lock, select, true { lock: replay took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock (TRUNCATE, DROP, ALTER TABLE, or VACUUM truncating a table's empty tail, which ALTER TABLE ... SET (vacuum_truncate = off) stops).} other {}}{adv_snapshot, select, true { snapshot: replay removed rows a standby query could still see (VACUUM on the primary). hot_standby_feedback = on keeps them on the primary, at the cost of bloat there.} other {}}{adv_tablespace, select, true { tablespace: replay dropped a tablespace that standby queries used for temporary files; point temp_tablespaces elsewhere on the standby.} other {}}{has_advice, select, true {} other { }}
advisor.standby.recovery_conflicts.remed: Raise max_standby_streaming_delay (and max_standby_archive_delay) on the standby to let queries finish before replay cancels them, at the cost of the standby falling behind while they run; or remove the cause on the primary, as the detail says per reason.
advisor.standby.replay_paused.title: WAL replay is paused on this standby
advisor.standby.replay_paused.detail: The standby receives WAL but does not apply it, so its queries see ever older data, and the WAL it has not replayed accumulates in its pg_wal. Replay pauses on pg_wal_replay_pause(), and when recovery reaches a target with recovery_target_action = 'pause'.
advisor.standby.replay_paused.remediatio: Once the reason for the pause is over, resume replay as a superuser: SELECT pg_wal_replay_resume();
advisor.wal.directory_large.title: pg_wal holds {size}, more than max_wal_size and wal_keep_size explain
advisor.wal.directory_large.detail: pg_wal holds {size} in {files} files, more than twice max_wal_size ({max_wal}) plus wal_keep_size ({keep}). Something keeps WAL the checkpoints would remove: a replication slot whose consumer is behind or gone, a failing archive_command, or a standby that needs it.{has_archive, select, true { {archive_ready} segments wait for archive_command, which keeps them until it succeeds.} other {}} When the disk fills, the server stops.
advisor.wal.directory_large.remediation: Look at the WAL each replication slot retains (pg_replication_slots, the cluster's slots) and drop the slots no consumer uses with pg_drop_replication_slot(); fix archive_command if segments wait for it (pg_stat_archiver.last_failed_wal).
